description: How EAGLE components are built and managed: library structure (symbols, footprints, 3D packages, device sets with gates, package variants, connects, technologies, prefixes, value mode and attributes), managed libraries with URNs, library update and replace, 3D package commands, the Fusion links (FUSIONSYNC, FUSIONTEAM, EXPORTSTEP), the manufacturing flyout, design blocks, the libraries shipped with EAGLE 9.6.0 and the product's retirement in June 2026.

tools.name: Library file (.lbr) contents
tools.description: An EAGLE library holds four kinds of objects: footprints (the land pattern placed on the board), 3D packages (a model or box linked to one or more footprints), symbols (the schematic graphic with pins) and device sets, which tie one or more symbols (gates) to footprints through package variants and pin-to-pad connects. A library may also contain packageless devices such as supply symbols and drawing frames, or only footprints (usable only in the Layout Editor).
tools.usage: OPEN <name>.lbr (or File > New > Library); the XML sections are <packages>, <packages3d>, <symbols>, <devicesets>
tools.example:
OPEN mylib.lbr
EDIT R-10.fpt      # footprint
EDIT R.sym         # symbol
EDIT R.dev         # device set
tools.notes: Before EAGLE 9.1 footprints were called packages; 'package' remains valid in scripts and ULPs (UL_PACKAGE and the new alias UL_FOOTPRINT). Schematics and boards embed copies of all library objects they use, so they can be passed on without the libraries.

tools.name: Symbol
tools.description: The schematic representation of a component or of one gate of it. It contains pins (placed and named with PIN and NAME, with direction, function, length and visibility set by CHANGE) and drawing objects, plus the placeholder texts >NAME and >VALUE that show the actual part name and value. A symbol may be used by many device sets.
tools.usage: Library Editor > Symbol (EDIT <name>.sym); commands PIN, NAME, CHANGE, LINE, TEXT
tools.example:
EDIT OPAMP.sym
GRID MIL 100
PIN 'IN+' In Short R0 (-400 100)
PIN 'IN-' In Short R0 (-400 -100)
PIN 'OUT' Out Short R180 (400 0)
LAYER 95; TEXT '>NAME' (0 300)
LAYER 96; TEXT '>VALUE' (0 -300)
tools.notes: Keep pins on the 0.1 inch grid so nets connect. Pins can be pasted from a text or spreadsheet list since 8.7 (COPY from the source document, then PASTE in the Symbol Editor).

tools.name: Footprint (package)
tools.description: The board land pattern of a component: pads (through-hole) and smds, outlines in tPlace/tDocu, >NAME and >VALUE texts in tNames/tValues, and optional keepout/restrict areas. Before EAGLE 9.1 footprints were called packages, and many commands and file sections still use that word.
tools.usage: Library Editor > Footprint (EDIT <name>.fpt or .pac); commands PAD, SMD, PADARRAY, SMDARRAY, LINE, TEXT
tools.notes: Library convention: tNames holds names, tPlace the silkscreen, tDocu documentation graphics that are not printed on the board; t/bRestrict and t/bKeepout block tracks and components. Package-only libraries such as ref-packages are usable only in the Layout Editor.

tools.name: Device set and device names
tools.description: A device set is the master definition of a component: its gates (symbols), package variants (footprint plus optional 3D package), connects, technologies, prefix, value mode, attributes and description. The full device name is built from the device set name, the technology and the variant name: '*' in the set name is replaced by the technology and '?' by the variant; otherwise both are appended (technology first).
tools.usage: Library Editor > Device (EDIT <name>.dev); ADD, PACKAGE, CONNECT, TECHNOLOGY, PREFIX, VALUE, ATTRIBUTE, DESCRIPTION
tools.example:
EDIT 74*00.dev
PACKAGE DIL14 N
TECHNOLOGY -* '' LS HCT
# devices: 7400N, 74LS00N, 74HCT00N
tools.notes: A device set is called a device when it has only one variant. In XML: <deviceset name prefix uservalue urn> with <gates>, <devices> and an optional <spice> mapping.

tools.name: Gates, swaplevel and addlevel
tools.description: Each symbol added to a device set becomes a gate with a name, a swaplevel and an addlevel. Swaplevel 0 means not swappable; equal non-zero values allow GATESWAP between equivalent gates, even across devices. Addlevel controls how gates appear in the schematic: Next (fetched one after another by ADD), Must (always present, deleted with the last gate), Always (like Must but deletable and recallable with INVOKE), Can (only via INVOKE when Next gates exist) and Request (only via INVOKE and not counted, typical for power gates).
tools.usage: In the device editor: ADD <symbol> [gate_name] [swaplevel] [NEXT|MUST|ALWAYS|CAN|REQUEST] •; change later with CHANGE SWAPLEVEL / CHANGE ADDLEVEL
tools.example:
EDIT 74*00.dev
ADD NAND A 1 NEXT (0 0)
ADD NAND B 1 NEXT (0 -10)
ADD NAND C 1 NEXT (0 -20)
ADD NAND D 1 NEXT (0 -30)
ADD PWRN PWR 0 REQUEST (20 0)
tools.notes: With Request power gates a single-gate part is named IC1 instead of IC1A; parts with several Next gates get names like IC1A..IC1D.

tools.name: Package variants (PACKAGE in the device editor)
tools.description: A package variant pairs a footprint (and optionally a 3D package) with a variant name inside a device set; each variant has its own connects, technologies and attributes. PACKAGE without arguments opens a selection dialog; with arguments it creates, renames, deletes or re-targets variants, can take the footprint from another library, and can create variants from a 3D package or its URN (downloading it if needed).
tools.usage: PACKAGE pname vname | PACKAGE pname.fpt vname | PACKAGE pname.p3d vname | PACKAGE urn vname | PACKAGE pname@lname vname | PACKAGE -old new | PACKAGE -name | PACKAGE @vname [pname|urn]
tools.example:
EDIT LM358.dev
PACKAGE SO08@ref-packages D
PACKAGE DIL08 N
PACKAGE @D SO08.fpt   # swap the footprint of variant D, keep its connects
tools.notes: In a schematic or board, PACKAGE behaves like CHANGE PACKAGE. Use CONNECT after creating a variant; BOARD later uses the variant's footprint.

tools.name: Connects (CONNECT, pin-to-pad mapping)
tools.description: CONNECT defines which pad of the footprint belongs to which pin of which gate for the current package variant. One pin can go to several pads: ALL (default) requires every pad to be wired on the board, ANY lets any of them carry the signal so the part's internal connection may act as a bridge. Without arguments a dialog opens.
tools.usage: CONNECT [ALL|ANY] gate.pin pad .. | CONNECT [ALL|ANY] pin pad ..  (several pads in single quotes: '1 3 5')
tools.notes: Giving all connections in one CONNECT call is much faster for large parts. A device is only complete for BOARD when every pin is connected (SET CHECK_CONNECTS).

tools.name: Technologies (TECHNOLOGY)
tools.description: Technologies are name variants of a device that share symbols, footprint and connects but differ in part of the name, such as the TTL families L, LS or HCT, and each technology can carry its own attribute values. The chosen technology replaces '*' in the device set name (or is appended). TECHNOLOGY needs a package variant selected first.
tools.usage: TECHNOLOGY name ..; | TECHNOLOGY -name ..; | TECHNOLOGY -* ..;   ('' = empty technology)
tools.example:
EDIT 74*00.dev
PACKAGE N
TECHNOLOGY -* '' L LS S HCT;
# 7400 74L00 74LS00 74S00 74HCT00
tools.notes: Only ASCII 33..126 is allowed; lowercase is converted to uppercase. In schematics and boards TECHNOLOGY acts like CHANGE TECHNOLOGY; a changed value survives a later CHANGE TECHNOLOGY.

tools.name: Prefix (PREFIX)
tools.description: The prefix of a device set sets the leading characters of automatically generated part names when the device is added to a schematic (R1, R2, IC1 ...). In a module sheet PREFIX sets the prefix of module instances. Names can be changed later with NAME.
tools.usage: PREFIX prefix_string;   (device editor or module sheet)
tools.notes: Stored as the prefix attribute of <deviceset>. renumber-sheet.ulp uses the device set prefix when renumbering parts.

tools.name: Value on/off (VALUE in the device editor)
tools.description: In the device editor VALUE ON lets the user enter a free value in the schematic (resistors, capacitors: the part is not fully specified until a value is set), while VALUE OFF makes the device name including technology and variant the value (for example 74LS00N); the user can still override it after a confirmation. A value changed by hand is kept even if the technology or package variant is changed later with CHANGE PACKAGE or CHANGE TECHNOLOGY.
tools.usage: VALUE ON; | VALUE OFF;   (device editor)  -  stored as uservalue="yes|no" in <deviceset>
tools.notes: In schematics and boards VALUE sets part values (VALUE R1 10k R2 100k); only the default assembly variant can be changed with VALUE, other variants use VARIANT.

tools.name: Device attributes (ATTRIBUTE in libraries)
tools.description: Attributes are name/value pairs attached per technology of a device (for example manufacturer, part number, POPULARITY). They are variable by default, so the schematic can overwrite them, or constant, which protects them (a library UPDATE resets constant values). Parts can get extra attributes in the schematic and elements in the board; '*' defines global attributes.
tools.usage: ATTRIBUTE name ['value'] [variable|constant|delete]   (library)  |  ATTRIBUTE part name 'value'  |  ATTRIBUTE * name 'value'
tools.example:
EDIT PINHD-1X4.dev
ATTRIBUTE MPN 'HDR-1X4-254' constant
ATTRIBUTE POPULARITY '91'
tools.notes: Names are case-insensitive and may contain letters, digits, _ # and -. POPULARITY (0-100, 9.5+) feeds the popularity filter of the ADD dialog. Show attributes on symbols with >ATTRNAME texts.

tools.name: Packageless, supply and external devices
tools.description: Devices without a PACKAGE are schematic-only: drawing frames, documentation symbols, supply symbols (one symbol with a Sup pin, as in supply1/supply2) and external devices. External devices may have pins but must carry the _EXTERNAL_ attribute defined in the library; they document things added outside the board, such as simulation sources and probes. Once a package is assigned, the device is treated as a normal part again.
tools.usage: Device set with gates and technologies but no PACKAGE; external: ATTRIBUTE _EXTERNAL_ ''
tools.example:
EDIT TESTSOURCE.dev
ADD SOURCE G$1 0 NEXT (0 0)   # a symbol with pins, no PACKAGE
ATTRIBUTE _EXTERNAL_ ''
WRITE
tools.notes: Saving such a device creates a variant with an empty name. Supply symbols are needed for automatic supply connections (see supply1.lbr description).

tools.name: Creating a library device (workflow)
tools.description: The built-in help's three-step recipe for a new component, each step building on the previous: create the footprint (grid, named pads/smds, >NAME/>VALUE, outline), create the symbol (named pins with parameters, >NAME/>VALUE, outline), then create the device (assign footprint and optional 3D package with PACKAGE, add gates with ADD, map pins to pads with CONNECT) and save. Open the library with File > Open/New, not with USE.
tools.usage: OPEN lib.lbr > EDIT x.fpt (PAD/SMD/TEXT/LINE) > EDIT x.sym (PIN/NAME/CHANGE/TEXT/LINE) > EDIT x.dev (PACKAGE/ADD/CONNECT/PREFIX/VALUE) > WRITE; then USE lib.lbr in the editors
tools.example:
OPEN mylib.lbr
EDIT R-10.fpt; GRID MIL 50; PAD '1' (-200 0); PAD '2' (200 0)
EDIT R.sym; PIN '1' Pas Short R0 (-200 0); PIN '2' Pas Short R180 (200 0)
EDIT R.dev; ADD R G$1 0 NEXT (0 0); PACKAGE R-10 ''; CONNECT G$1.1 1 G$1.2 2; PREFIX R; VALUE ON
WRITE
tools.notes: Newer helpers: PINARRAY/PADARRAY/SMDARRAY (9.2), the Package Generator (LAUNCH PACKAGE3D-GENERATOR) and make-symbol-device-package-bsdl.ulp for large parts.

tools.name: Library Editor table of contents
tools.description: The first view of an open library: columns listing devices, footprints, 3D packages and symbols, where objects are opened, renamed, deleted, duplicated or described. Selecting a device highlights the footprints and symbols it uses; context menus offer Used packages/symbols and Using DeviceSets, plus adding a device to the open schematic or a footprint to the board. Add buttons create new objects or import them; Import 3D Package imports from another library, adds one from the web or starts the package generator.
tools.usage: Library Editor > Table of Contents icon (action toolbar); Library menu > Description / Table of Contents / Manage Devices-Symbols-Packages / Remove / Rename / Update
tools.example: OPEN mylib.lbr   # table of contents opens; double-click R.dev to edit, right-click R-10 > Using DeviceSets
tools.notes: Since 9.5 several devices, footprints, symbols or 3D packages can be selected and deleted together (not undoable).

tools.name: Edit Library Object dialog and importing objects
tools.description: The dialog behind the Device/Footprint/Symbol icons: type a name in the New field to create an object or open an existing one, or click Import... to copy a device, footprint or symbol from any library in use into the open library (importing a device also brings its 3D packages, footprints and symbols). Devices and packages can also be dragged from the Control Panel tree into the Library Editor; same-named objects are updated.
tools.usage: Library Editor > Device|Footprint|Symbol icon > New: <name> | Import...;  EDIT name.dev|.fpt|.sym|urn
tools.example:
EDIT LM317.dev   # creates the device if it does not exist
# or: Device icon > Import... > v-reg > LM317TS
tools.notes: Since 9.4 COPY can copy devices, symbols, footprints and packages from a design file into a library, and design-file context menus offer copying assets into a library.

tools.name: Managed libraries
tools.description: Managed libraries are identified by a server-assigned URN and a version number stored with every part placed from them, so updates always use the right library even if several libraries share a name; 3D package references require them. The libraries shipped with EAGLE are managed (and not meant to be edited): copy devices into your own library and turn it into a managed one (Control Panel > right-click > Create managed library), which appears under My Managed Libraries. Since 9.5 managed folders on library.io can be shared with invited users.
tools.usage: Control Panel > Libraries > Managed Libraries / My Managed Libraries; right-click a library > Create managed library | Copy to Another Managed Folder; INFO on a part shows library version and URN
tools.example: Right-click lbr\mylib.lbr > Create managed library, then click View on Web to assign 3D packages; later: UPDATE 'urn:adsk.eagle:library:<id>'
tools.notes: To migrate an existing design, UPDATE it from the managed library with the same name; parts from a same-named unmanaged library must then be replaced individually. EAGLE backs up the local library file before downloading a new version. Creating, downloading and updating managed libraries depends on Autodesk online services, which were part of the retired product; do not rely on them without checking.

tools.name: Library URNs (urn:adsk.eagle:...)
tools.description: Managed assets are referenced by URNs of the form urn:adsk.eagle:<type>:<id>[/<version>], where type is library, component, symbol, footprint or package (3D package). The version suffix is omitted when referring to the asset in general. Schematics and boards store library_urn, package3d_urn and override URNs on parts and elements, plus library_version and library_locally_modified.
tools.usage: urn:adsk.eagle:library:<id> | urn:adsk.eagle:component:<id>/<ver> | urn:adsk.eagle:package:<id>/<ver>; accepted by UPDATE, ADD ... P3D=, PACKAGE, REPLACE ... P3D= and EDIT urn
tools.example:
ADD PINHD-1X4@pinhead P3D=urn:adsk.eagle:package:22404/2
UPDATE 'urn:adsk.eagle:library:42';
tools.notes: Format documented in doc/eagle.dtd. Managed libraries with different URNs are never matched by UPDATE even if their names are equal.

tools.name: Library Manager (Library > Manage Libraries)
tools.description: Dialog for choosing which libraries a design uses and for downloading or updating web-based libraries. Tabs: In Use (libraries listed in the ADD dialog), Available (not in use) and, since 9.0, In Design (libraries referenced by the open schematic/board). Buttons Use, Remove, Update, Edit and Delete; since 9.4 bundled managed libraries can be removed and re-installed.
tools.usage: Schematic/Board Editor > Library > Manage Libraries...   (text equivalent for the in-use list: USE)
tools.example:
Library > Manage Libraries > Available > select ngspice-simulation > Use
# script equivalents: USE mylib.lbr;  USE urn:adsk.eagle:library:462;  USE -*;
tools.notes: A banner appears when a design references libraries that can be downloaded or updated. The Control Panel's green/grey marker also toggles 'in use'.

tools.name: Updating parts from libraries (UPDATE)
tools.description: Compares the parts of a schematic/board with their library objects and replaces changed ones. Without arguments a dialog selects the library; 'UPDATE;' checks all libraries; names, paths or URNs restrict it; 'old = new' re-targets a design library to another library and renames it. +@/-@ append or strip @<number> to freeze local library names. In the Library Editor UPDATE refreshes the footprints of the loaded library from other libraries.
tools.usage: UPDATE | UPDATE; | UPDATE library_name..; | UPDATE footprint@library..; | UPDATE +@|-@ [libs]; | UPDATE old_library_name = new_library_name;
tools.notes: Acts on both schematic and board when annotation is active. Gates, pins and pads are matched by name or coordinates; a pin both renamed and moved cannot be updated in one step. Always run ERC and DRC afterwards. exp-lbrs.ulp exports a design's libraries for editing before an UPDATE.

tools.name: Replacing devices and footprints (REPLACE)
tools.description: Swaps the device of a part for a compatible one (same used gates and connected pins/pads by name or coordinates), even from another library, and can pick the 3D package with P3D=. In a board without schematic it replaces footprints: SET REPLACE_SAME NAMES (default) requires equal pad names, SET REPLACE_SAME COORDS equal pad positions.
tools.usage: REPLACE [device_name[@library_name] [P3D=3d_package]] • .. | REPLACE part_name device_name[@library] [P3D=..] | REPLACE element_name footprint_name
tools.example:
REPLACE R1 R-EU_0207/10@rcl
REPLACE JP1 PINHD-1X4@pinhead P3D=1X04/90
tools.notes: Needs the tOrigins/bOrigins layer visible. It updates library objects as necessary, which can change other parts too; run ERC and DRC afterwards.

tools.name: Bundled managed-library cache (cache\lbr, libraries.json)
tools.description: The folder <EAGLE>\cache\lbr holds snapshots of the managed libraries as of the 9.6.0 release (259 top-level libraries listed in libraries.json with id, author 'Eagle Pcb', name, version and URN flag), plus the non-managed subfolders elektro and seeed. At start-up EAGLE imports each snapshot into the local managed-library cache unless a newer version is already there.
tools.usage: C:\Program Files\EAGLE 9.6.0\cache\lbr\*.lbr; libraries.json; Control Panel > Libraries
tools.example: {"id":527439,"author":"Eagle Pcb","name":"ngspice-simulation","version":18,"has_urns":true,...}
tools.notes: The .lbr files are plain XML (eagle.dtd) and can be read without EAGLE, e.g. to extract device sets, footprints, attributes and 3D package URNs.

tools.name: 3D packages (PACKAGE3D)
tools.description: A 3D package is a managed 3D representation (type model, e.g. a STEP model, or box) that references one or more footprints; device variants list their 3D packages as package3dinstances. Managed libraries originally got simple boxes that can be replaced with STEP models in the web editor, and the 3D packages are used by the Fusion ECAD/MCAD link. ADD, REPLACE and PACKAGE accept a 3D package by name or URN.
tools.usage: ADD device[@lib] P3D=<3d name|urn> | REPLACE ... P3D=... | PACKAGE <name>.p3d vname | Library Editor > Import 3D Package; ULP object UL_PACKAGE3D
tools.example:
ADD PINHD-1X4@pinhead P3D=1X04/90
# XML: <package3d name="1X04/90" urn="urn:adsk.eagle:package:22404/2" type="model">
tools.notes: Copying a 3D package into another library keeps its URN (8.7). A 3D package copied into a library is added to device variants that use its footprint and have none (9.2). Assigning or editing 3D models needs Autodesk's online services.

tools.name: LAUNCH PACKAGE3D-GENERATOR
tools.description: Launches the web-based Package Generator, which builds a footprint and a matching 3D package from package parameters (SMD land patterns intended to follow IPC-7351B), or the 3D package web search. In the device editor it creates a new device variant (like PACKAGE); in the library editor it imports a package (like COPY).
tools.usage: LAUNCH PACKAGE3D-GENERATOR [managed_folder_id] | LAUNCH PACKAGE3D-WEB-SEARCH

parameters.name: managed_folder_id
parameters.description: Target managed folder; if omitted and several hubs are writable, a folder selection dialog appears.

tools.example:
EDIT MYCHIP.dev
LAUNCH PACKAGE3D-GENERATOR   # generate a QFN footprint + 3D model as a new variant
tools.notes: Web-based: requires Autodesk online services. Generated models could also be downloaded as STEP or OBJ (8.7 notes).

tools.name: CUSTOM3D
tools.description: Assigns a custom 3D package to a part or element in the schematic or board. The custom model overrides the part's library 3D package in the Fusion ECAD/MCAD process and is stored as override_package3d_urn on the part.
tools.usage: CUSTOM3D   (then left-click the part/element)
tools.example:
CUSTOM3D
# click U1, choose or create the custom 3D package
tools.notes: Added in 9.4. Edit it with EDIT3D, remove it with OVERRIDEREMOVE.

tools.name: EDIT3D
tools.description: Opens the managed 3D package of a part or element for editing. If the part has a custom override (from CUSTOM3D), that custom 3D package is edited instead of the library one.
tools.usage: EDIT3D   (then left-click the part/element)
tools.example:
EDIT3D
# click J1 to adjust its 3D package
tools.notes: Added in 9.4; relies on the web-based 3D package editor.

tools.name: OVERRIDEREMOVE
tools.description: Removes an overridden (custom) 3D package from an element or part in the board or schematic editor, so the part falls back to the 3D package of its library device. Use it to undo a CUSTOM3D assignment.
tools.usage: OVERRIDEREMOVE   (then left-click the element/part)
tools.example:
OVERRIDEREMOVE
# click U1: its CUSTOM3D model is dropped
tools.notes: Called REMOVEOVERRIDE in the 9.4 release notes; the command name in 9.6 help is OVERRIDEREMOVE.

tools.name: PAINTROLLER
tools.description: Transfers selected properties of one object to other objects of the same type, like a format painter. Click the source object, tick the properties to copy in the Copy Properties dialog, confirm with OK and click the target objects.
tools.usage: PAINTROLLER • | PAINTROLLER • • | PAINTROLLER • [propertyname] •
tools.example:
PAINTROLLER
# click a 0.4 mm trace, tick Width, OK, then click the traces to widen
tools.notes: Added in 9.2; also available as an icon in the command toolbar.

tools.name: MANUFACTURING
tools.description: Board-editor command for the manufacturing flyout and CAM exporter. Without parameters it toggles the manufacturing flyout (live board preview with dimensions, drill maps and other views); MANUFACTURING CAM opens the CAM Processor dialog and MANUFACTURING EXPORT writes a ZIP archive with Gerber and Excellon data for the current design.
tools.usage: MANUFACTURING; | MANUFACTURING CAM; | MANUFACTURING EXPORT;
tools.example: MANUFACTURING EXPORT;   # one-click Gerber + Excellon ZIP for a standard layer stack
tools.notes: Board editor only (8.6+). Preview resolution is adjustable and the Gerber preview can be saved as an image (8.7). For headless output use eaglecon -X -dCAMJOB instead, which still works after the licensing shutdown.

tools.name: FUSIONSYNC
tools.description: Links a board to a Fusion (360) PCB model to create its 3D representation and synchronise in both directions: push EAGLE changes to Fusion, or pull and merge mechanical changes made in Fusion (board outline, holes, component positions). The link is stored in the board file; the FUSIONSYNC flyout turns red when the designs are out of sync.
tools.usage: FUSIONSYNC   (or the FUSIONSYNC flyout in the Layout Editor: choose/create Fusion project > Push to Fusion... / Pull from Fusion / View on Web)
tools.example:
FUSIONSYNC
# choose an existing Fusion project with a PCB feature, Push to Fusion, later Pull from Fusion, then DRC
tools.notes: Stored as <fusionsync> in the board XML. Parts without 3D packages show up without proper 3D bodies. Needs Autodesk cloud services and a signed-in editor; after June 2026 Fusion's Electronics workspace, which opens EAGLE files directly, is the practical route.

tools.name: FUSIONTEAM
tools.description: Publishes the schematic and/or board and, via a chosen CAM job, a zipped set of manufacturing files to Fusion Team, where others can view (including a 3D board view), share and comment on the design in a browser without EAGLE or Fusion installed. It is started from the Fusion Team tab of the Layout Editor or by typing the command, and a dialog selects the files and the Fusion Team location.
tools.usage: FUSIONTEAM   (or the Fusion Team tab in the Layout Editor; tab visibility in Options/User interface)
tools.example:
FUSIONTEAM
# select board + schematic, CAM job example_2_layer.cam, target project folder, Publish
tools.notes: Added in 9.3; stored as <fusionteam> in the design XML. Depends on Autodesk cloud services.

tools.name: EXPORTSTEP
tools.description: Exports the board as a STEP model. The translation runs through the Fusion Sync cloud service; the resulting file is listed under Recent Generated 3D files on the Control Panel home tab, where a click opens its folder.
tools.usage: EXPORTSTEP   (or Layout Editor > File > Export > STEP)
tools.example:
EXPORTSTEP
# then Control Panel > Home > Recent Generated 3D files > click the entry
tools.notes: Added in 9.2. Not an offline exporter: without the cloud service no STEP file is produced. Alternatives: eagleidfexporter.ulp / generate-3d-idf-data.ulp (IDF) or opening the board in Fusion Electronics.

tools.name: Design blocks (.dbl)
tools.description: A design block is a reusable circuit stored as a .dbl XML file containing a schematic, a board or ideally a consistent pair, with an HTML description and attributes. WRITE DBL saves the current design (or, via File > Save selection as Design Block, a consistent selection) as a block; PASTE DBL or the Control Panel's Add to schematic/board inserts it, pasting schematic and board parts together when a consistent pair is open.
tools.usage: WRITE DBL [name] | PASTE DBL [orientation] [offset] [filename] • | EDIT name.dbl (preview) | EDIT name.dbl; (open in the design block editors)
tools.example:
WRITE DBL 'D:/blocks/ldo-3v3.dbl'
PASTE DBL 'LDO-MCP1703DB-5V0-3V3.dbl' (50 50)
tools.notes: A single-sheet block pasted in the schematic is placed on the current sheet; from the board new sheets are added. Combined schematic/board selection is not supported in hierarchical schematics. Shipped blocks are under examples\design blocks\examples.

tools.name: EAGLE retirement (7 June 2026)
tools.description: Autodesk stopped selling and supporting EAGLE on 7 June 2026 and shut down its licensing servers. Since then the EAGLE editors stop at the Autodesk 'Sign in' window, while the command-line CAM Processor (eaglecon -X) still produces manufacturing data from existing boards (checked on 9.6.0 in September 2026). Autodesk Fusion's Electronics workspace is the successor and opens EAGLE files; Altium Designer, OrCAD, KiCad and others can import them.
tools.usage: Headless output: eaglecon -X -dCAMJOB -j<job.cam> -o<dir> <board>.brd;  migration: open .sch/.brd/.lbr in Fusion Electronics or import them into another ECAD tool
tools.example: eaglecon -X -N -dCAMJOB -jexample_2_layer.cam -oD:\out board.brd
tools.notes: Features that rely on Autodesk online services (managed-library downloads, 3D package editing, FUSIONSYNC, FUSIONTEAM, EXPORTSTEP) should be treated as unavailable unless verified. For eaglecon the -o output directory must already exist. The XML design and library files (eagle.dtd) remain readable by any program.

tools.name: Passive component libraries (rcl, resistor-*, capacitor-wima, pot, varistor, fuse ...)
tools.description: Generic and vendor passives: rcl.lbr (resistors, capacitors and inductors with about 490 3D packages, e.g. R-EU_, R-US_, C-EU), resistor-bourns, resistor-dil, resistor-net, resistor-power, resistor-shunt, resistor-sil, capacitor-wima, pot and piher (potentiometers), ptc-ntc, varistor (varistors/thermistors), fuse, jumper and jump-0r-smd (solder jumpers). rcl.lbr covers the common resistor, capacitor and inductor footprints from 0402 SMD to large through-hole types, and its device sets accept user values (VALUE ON).
tools.usage: ADD <device>@<library>, e.g. ADD R-EU_0204/7@rcl
tools.example:
ADD R-EU_0204/7@rcl R1 R0 (10 10)
ADD C-EUC0805@rcl C1 R90 (20 10)
VALUE R1 10k C1 100n
tools.notes: All shipped in <EAGLE>\cache\lbr as managed libraries.

tools.name: Inductor, transformer, filter and crystal libraries
tools.description: Magnetics and frequency parts: inductors (inductors and filters), inductor-coilcraft, inductor-neosid, inductor-nkl, trafo, trafo-hammondmfg, trafo-siemens, trafo-xicon, lc-filter, murata-filter, johanson-technology (filters), crystal, crystal-geyer_V1_0 and IQD-Frequency-Products (crystals and oscillators). Most of them include 3D packages for their footprints.
tools.usage: ADD <device>@<library>
tools.example: ADD *@crystal   # browse crystals and resonators in the ADD dialog
tools.notes: Wildcards in ADD open the tree view of matching devices.

tools.name: Discrete semiconductor libraries (diode, rectifier, transistor*, triac ...)
tools.description: Diodes and transistors: diode (about 200 device sets), rectifier, transistor, transistor-fet, transistor-neu-to92, transistor-npn, transistor-pnp, transistor-power, transistor-small-signal, triac (thyristors, triacs, trigger diodes), zetex (power MOSFETs, bridges, diodes), ir (International Rectifier), discrete (antenna, arrester, thermistor) and semicon-smd-ipc (IPC SMD semiconductors). Use them for real board parts; simulation-only models are in the separate ngspice-simulation library.
tools.usage: ADD <device>@<library>
tools.example:
ADD BAT42@diode D1 R0 (30 10)
ADD 2N3055*@transistor-power
tools.notes: For simulation use the pre-mapped DIODE/BJT/FET parts of ngspice-simulation or map these with ADDMODEL.

tools.name: Optoelectronics and display libraries (led, opto*, optocoupler, display-*)
tools.description: LEDs, displays and opto parts: led, led-lumiled, lumiled, led-7-segment, display-hp, display-kingbright, display-lcd, opto-honeywell, opto-honeywell-3000, opto-honeywell-4000, opto-trans-siemens, opto-transmittter-hp, opto-vishay, optocoupler, photo-elements, fiber-optic-hp and toshiba (fiber-optic devices). The display libraries cover HP and Kingbright LED displays and LCD modules from Hitachi, Data Modul and Tuxgraphics.
tools.usage: ADD <device>@<library>
tools.example: ADD TOPLED-3@led LED1 R0 (40 10)
tools.notes: Library names are spelled as shipped (opto-transmittter-hp has three t's).

tools.name: Logic family libraries (40xx, 45xx, 74xx-*, ecl, uln-udn ...)
tools.description: Standard logic: 40xx and 45xx (CMOS), 41xx, 74xx-us (US symbols) and 74xx-eu (European symbols) with over 300 device sets each, 74ttl-din (DIN symbols), 74ac-logic, 74xx-little-us and 74xx-little-de (single/dual gates), 751xx and texas-sn55-sn75, ecl, fifo and uln-udn (driver arrays). Device sets use '*' for technologies, e.g. 74*00.
tools.usage: ADD 74<tech><type><variant>@<library>
tools.example:
ADD 74LS00N@74xx-us IC1 (0 0)
# places gate IC1A; ADD again or INVOKE for B-D and the power gate
tools.notes: Power pins are usually in a separate Request gate (see 'Gates, swaplevel and addlevel').

tools.name: Analog, interface and power IC libraries by manufacturer
tools.description: Vendor IC libraries: linear (op-amps, comparators, regulators, ADC/DAC; over 330 device sets), analog-devices, burr-brown, linear-technology, maxim (over 440 device sets), texas, exar, allegro, national-semiconductor, on-semiconductor, st-microelectronics, micrel, sipex, rohm, infineon, cirrus-logic, gennum, holtek, philips-semiconductors, fairchild-semic, telefunken, lsi-computer-systems, avago, micronas, halo-electronics and lem (current sensors). Many were created by the CadSoft librarian long ago, so verify footprints and pinouts against current data sheets.
tools.usage: ADD <device>@<library>
tools.example: ADD LM358*@linear IC2
tools.notes: Use the ADD dialog search (with Description ticked) to find parts across libraries.

tools.name: Microcontroller, processor and programmable-logic libraries
tools.description: MCUs and CPUs: atmel (AVR and memories), microchip (PIC), micro-fujitsu, micro-harris, micro-hitachi, micro-intel, micro-mc68000, micro-motorola, micro-philips, micro-renesas, micro-siemens, cypress (EZ-USB), silabs (C8051F), stm32xx, freescale, infineon-tricore, zilog, ftdichip, plxtech (PCI 9056), etx-board. Programmable logic: altera, altera-cyclone-II, altera-stratix-iv, xilinx-xcv, amd-mach, pld-intel, wafer-scale-psd.
tools.usage: ADD <device>@<library>
tools.example: ADD TINY10*@atmel U1
tools.notes: Large pin-count parts are good candidates for make-symbol-device-package-bsdl.ulp when a library part is missing.

tools.name: Memory libraries (memory, memory-*, am29-memory)
tools.description: Memories: memory (generic), memory-hitachi, memory-idt (about 300 device sets), memory-micron (flash), memory-motorola-dram, memory-nec, memory-sram and am29-memory (AMD flash). They include EPROM, flash, static RAM and DRAM devices from several manufacturers.
tools.usage: ADD <device>@<library>
tools.example: ADD 2764*@memory U3
tools.notes: Most are legacy parts; check availability before using them in new designs.

tools.name: Connector libraries (con-*, pinhead, 19inch, busbar)
tools.description: About 75 connector libraries: pin headers (pinhead, con-lstb male, con-lsta female, con-garry), terminal blocks (con-phoenix-254/-3.81/-350/-500/-508/-762/-mkds_5/-smkdsp, con-wago, con-wago-500/-508, con-wago255, con-weidmueller-sl35, con-ptr500), vendor families (con-molex with over 260 device sets, con-amp*, con-samtec, con-hirose, con-jst, con-lumberg, con-harting*, con-3m, con-tyco ...), D-sub (con-subd), coax (con-coax), VG/DIN 41612 (con-vg), PC/104, CompactPCI and ribbon cable connectors, plus 19inch (Eurocards) and busbar. Search them with ADD and wildcards, e.g. ADD *@con-molex.
tools.usage: ADD <device>@<library>
tools.example:
ADD PINHD-1X4@pinhead JP1 R0 (0 0)
ADD MSTBV2@con-phoenix-508 X1
tools.notes: Many connector parts carry POPULARITY attributes (e.g. PINHD-1X4 = 91) used by the ADD dialog's popularity filter.

tools.name: Switch and relay libraries (switch*, relay)
tools.description: Switches: switch, switch-alps, switch-coto (reed), switch-dil (DIL and code switches), switch-misc, switch-omron, switch-raychem, switch-reed. Relays: relay (Eichhoff, Finder, Fujitsu, Hamlin, Omron, Matsushita/NAiS, Siemens, Schrack; over 260 device sets).
tools.usage: ADD <device>@<library>
tools.example: ADD D-TS@switch-omron S1
tools.notes: Use the preview in the ADD dialog to choose the right package variant; multi-gate parts need INVOKE for gates that are not placed automatically.

tools.name: Power supply and RF module libraries
tools.description: Power: v-reg (LM317 and other regulators), v-reg-micrel, dc-dc-converter, recom-international (LED drivers), traco-electronic (DC/DC converters), battery. RF and wireless: microwave (Hittite), minicircuits, linx, lprs (easyRadio), maxstream (XBee), rf-solutions, telecontrolli and trimble (GNSS modules).
tools.usage: ADD <device>@<library>
tools.example: ADD LM317TS@v-reg IC3
tools.notes: Design blocks such as the LM317M and MC33063 regulators offer complete sub-circuits.

tools.name: Mechanical, test and special-purpose libraries
tools.description: Holes and mechanics: holes (mounting holes/pads), heatsink, special-drill, 19inch; test and pads: testpad (test pins with TP_SIGNAL_NAME attribute), solpad, wirepad; special (7-segment displays, switches, heatsinks, crystals, transformers), smd-special; acoustics and sensors: buzzer, microphon, murata-sensor, motorola-sensor-driver; chip cards: chipcard-siemens, con-chipcard-iso7816. These parts serve the board's mechanics, testing and assembly rather than the circuit function.
tools.usage: ADD <device>@<library>
tools.example: ADD MOUNT-HOLE3.2@holes H1 (5 5)
tools.notes: special-drill notes that drills above 0.51602 inch must be drawn as a circle in layer 20 Dimension.

tools.name: Supply, frame and documentation libraries (supply1, supply2, frames, docu-dummy, logo)
tools.description: Helpers for drawings: supply1 and supply2 (GND, VCC, 0V, +5V, -5V ... supply symbols needed for automatic supply connections), frames (sheet and layout frames such as DINA4_L or A3L-LOC), docu-dummy (dummy symbols) and logo (electronic and EAGLE logos). Their device sets have no packages, but frames and logo also contain footprints that can be placed directly in a board.
tools.usage: ADD <device>@<library>
tools.example:
ADD DINA4_L@frames FRAME1 (0 0)
ADD GND@supply1 (20 0)
tools.notes: Supply devices have a single Sup pin and no package; the pin name defines the net that is wired automatically, and in supply1 the device names equal those pin names.

tools.name: Reference package libraries (ref-packages, ref-packages-3d, smd-ipc, ic-package)
tools.description: Package-only libraries without device sets: ref-packages and ref-packages-longpad (about 1500 3D packages each), ref-packages-3d (IPC-standard footprints with 3D models), smd-ipc (IPC standard SMD land patterns) and ic-package (IC packages and sockets). Use them as footprint sources when building devices or as board-only footprints.
tools.usage: PACKAGE <footprint>@ref-packages <variant> (device editor) | ADD <footprint>@smd-ipc (board editor)
tools.example:
EDIT MYREG.dev
PACKAGE SOT223@ref-packages ''
tools.notes: update-packages.ulp updates the current library's footprints from a reference package library.

tools.name: elektro libraries (German electrical-schematic symbols)
tools.description: Subfolder cache\lbr\elektro with libraries for electrical wiring diagrams (German descriptions): e-elektro-zeichnungsrahmen (frames with contact/signal cross-references), e-elektromechanische-antriebe, e-halbleiter, e-klemmen (terminals, feed-in and earthing), e-kondensatoren, e-lampen-signalisation, e-messfuehler, e-messinstrumente, e-motoren, e-motorschutzschalter, e-schalter, e-schuetze-relais, e-sicherungen, e-sps (PLC), e-spulen-transformatoren, e-steckverbinder, e-stromversorgungselemente, e-symbole and eib-busch-jaeger (EIB installation bus). They are not listed in libraries.json, i.e. they are ordinary (unmanaged) libraries.
tools.usage: USE elektro/*.lbr; ADD <device>@<library>; editor presets: SCRIPT elektro-init.scr
tools.example:
SCRIPT elektro-init.scr
ADD *@e-schalter
tools.notes: No 3D packages; many devices carry simple packages whose pad names are shown instead of pin names (see e-bauteil-erstellen.ulp). Companion ULPs: e-attributverwaltung, e-brueckenverwaltung, e-klemmenplan, e-makelist; example: projects\examples\elektro\stern-dreieck-anlauf.sch.

tools.name: seeed libraries (Seeed OPL)
tools.description: Subfolder cache\lbr\seeed with Seeed Studio's OPL libraries: Seeed-OPL-Antenna, -Button, -Capacitor, -Connector, -Crystal-Oscillator, -Diode, -Display, -fuse, -ic, -Inductor, -Moudle (modules), -Relay, -Resistor, -sensor, -Switch and -Transistor, plus the spreadsheet Seeed-OPL-for-customer-20151021.xlsx. The libraries are arranged by component category, from antennas to transistors.
tools.usage: USE seeed/*.lbr; ADD <device>@Seeed-OPL-<group>
tools.example: ADD *@Seeed-OPL-Resistor   # about 290 resistor device sets
tools.notes: Not managed and without 3D packages. The Seeed example projects embed their own library copies (e.g. Discrete, Connector) rather than referencing these files.
